name: Flat Rs 50,000/year
where: bottom of the observed paid market
comparable: Fedena Standard (₹50k, full ERP, unlimited users)
why: Matches Fedena's entry tier exactly while offering far less scope. Would be priced against a full ERP rather than against a niche tool.

name: Flat Rs 1,20,000/year
where: top of the observed Indian market
verdict: DEFENSIBLE ONLY AGAINST INCUMBENTS, NOT AGAINST ERP
why: Equal to IncubatX's entry tier and 20% above Fedena's full ERP. Needs a scope argument against ERP vendors that we currently cannot make.

name: Flat Rs 2-5 lakh/year
where: inside IncubatX Accelerator/Executive AI and NestLens Scale
verdict: ABOVE THE BRACKET ON MOST EVIDENCE
why: Defensible only against direct incubation-platform competitors, and it crosses the GeM ₹5 lakh reverse-auction threshold at the top of the band.

name: Per-user pricing
why: Institutions cap the seats that touch innovation data at a handful (Phase 2 found 25 roles, only 4 with documented budget authority). Per-user pricing would collapse ACV to a few thousand rupees. Note Zoho requires a 25-licence minimum for Lite seats - the same trap.

name: Institution + number of startups
mechanic: platform fee plus a fee per incubated startup tracked
where: matches how IncubatX and NestLens actually scale
comparable: IncubatX 'up to 4 cohorts'; NestLens 'scales with cohort size'
why: Aligns price with the thing the institution is actually measured on - the cohort. Directly parallels the SISFS scheme, which pays incubators 5% management fee on the grant value they administer.

name: Base platform + premium modules
mechanic: core subscription plus paid add-on modules
where: proven - IncubatX Media Kit ₹15k/mo; incuTrack add-ons
comparable: IncubatX Media Kit add-on; incuTrack Mentor Matching/Surveys/Events
why: Lets us enter low (Model A/B) and expand with the buyer instead of front-loading the whole price at the first committee meeting.
